_source.csprng: The platform test injects incrementingRandom(0): a CSPRNG stub returning 0x00,0x01,0x02,... across ONE stream shared by K_c (32 bytes -> 0x00..0x1f), then the key-slot IV (12 bytes -> 0x20..0x2b), then the document IV (12 bytes -> 0x2c..0x37). Production draws from SecureRandom; the injection point is the RandomBytes seam only.
_source.mnemonics: Public BIP-39 specification phrases (128-bit entropy). They are not real phrases and open no real vault.

parameters.bip39: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512(NFKD(mnemonic), NFKD("mnemonic" + passphrase), 2048) -> 64 bytes, EMPTY passphrase
parameters.hkdfSalt: EMPTY / ABSENT - the RFC 5869 default (HashLen zero bytes), for BOTH uses
parameters.slotLayout: base64url(IV(12) || CT || TAG(16)), unpadded, AES-256-GCM under K_wrap
parameters.docAad: the EXACT wire header bytes, never a re-serialization

chain.mnemonic: abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about
chain.seedSource: The published BIP-39 empty-passphrase seed for the all-zero-entropy phrase; the platform derives it rather than pinning it. Kept so the chain has an intermediate checkpoint.

accountBinding.note: The platform test hard-codes the binding; the account id it hashes was recovered from deriveAccountBinding("vector-account") in the same file and re-verified against the constant.

envelope.note: BTVAULT1 || uint32BE(headerLength) || headerJson || ciphertext||tag. The plaintext is rawDeflate(utf8(documentJson)) (fflate 0.8.3), encrypted AES-256-GCM under K_c with the exact headerJson bytes as AAD.

tampersNote: The platform's 'fails closed for every binding header tamper and format rollback' set. Each entry replaces ONE header member and the GCM tag must refuse the envelope.

rotationSecondLeg.mnemonic: legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful legal winner thank yellow
rotationSecondLeg.note: The platform names this phrase as the rotation second leg but pins no bytes for it. Nothing is pinned here either - only the PROPERTIES the platform asserts (a different phrase and a different vault id derive a different K_wrap, and a different K_c derives a different fingerprint).
